proofs.proof_tex:
Let \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\) be the broader class in the proposed statement.  We first prove the upper bound on that class.  For \(n\geq5\), let \(m_j\) be the size of block \(j\) in \texttt{def:median-estimator}.  The block construction gives \(m_j\geq\lfloor n/5\rfloor\geq n/10\).  Apply inequality (13) from the proof of \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} to the block average, with \(m_j\) replacing the averaging sample size but with the prescribed full-sample threshold \(\lambda_n^\star\).  Every stochastic term is multiplied by at most \(\sqrt{n/m_j}\leq\sqrt{10}\), while every bias term is unchanged.  The comparisons (14)--(19), which use the full \(n\) appearing in \(\lambda_n^\star\) and \(\rho_n\), therefore imply a constant \(K<\infty\), uniform in \(j\), \(n\), the radius triple, and the member of \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\), such that
\[
E_P\!\left|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^\star}^{(j)}-\tau(P)\right|
\leq K\rho_n.                                           \qquad\text{(21)}
\]
The five blocks are independent by \texttt{ass:iid}.  Applying \texttt{lem:median-risk-upgrade} to (21) gives, for every \(u>0\),
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
P\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)\right|>u\right\}
\leq\min\{1,10(K\rho_n/u)^3\}.                         \qquad\text{(22)}
\]
For \(1\leq n<5\), \texttt{def:median-estimator} uses the full-sample clipped rule, and the broader-class conclusion of \texttt{thm:clipped-absolute-upper} gives
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
P\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{med}}-\tau(P)\right|
>C\rho_n/\alpha\right\}\leq\alpha.                    \qquad\text{(23)}
\]
Choose \(K_\alpha\geq K(10/\alpha)^{1/3}\) and also \(K_\alpha\geq C/\alpha\), with constants enlarged only as functions of \(\alpha\), \(\bar r\), and the retained fixed class constants.  Equations (22)--(23) and \texttt{def:bias-aware-interval} then give
\[
\inf_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}\geq1-\alpha,
\qquad
\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})
=2K_\alpha\rho_n.                                      \qquad\text{(24)}
\]
The center is measurable in \(O^{(n)}\), and its deterministic radius uses only the public certified radii and fixed constants.  Thus \texttt{def:interval-rule-class} gives \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\), and (24) proves the expected-length upper bound on \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\).

We now restrict to the nonempty reservoir-rich class \(\mathcal M_n\) and prove the converse.  The four component experiments certified by \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} are either two-point experiments or fuzzy two-prior experiments from \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{lb}}\); every fixed-sign law in them lies in \(\mathcal M_n\).  Consider first a two-point component with laws \(P_0,P_1\), targets separated by \(|\tau(P_1)-\tau(P_0)|=2d\), and product-law total variation at most \(\Gamma\).  If \(C_n\) is honest at both laws, then
\[
P_0\{\tau(P_0)\in C_n\}\geq1-\alpha,
\qquad
P_0\{\tau(P_1)\in C_n\}
\geq P_1\{\tau(P_1)\in C_n\}-\Gamma
\geq1-\alpha-\Gamma.
\]
A union bound and the fact that an interval containing both targets has length at least \(2d\) yield
\[
P_0\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq2d\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma.                                  \qquad\text{(25)}
\]

For a fuzzy component, let \(\overline P_-\) and \(\overline P_+\) be the two sample mixtures, with total variation at most \(\Gamma\), and let their prior target centers be separated by \(2d\).  The construction certified in \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} permits its finite cell count to be chosen so that, under either prior, the fixed-sign target is within \(d/4\) of its center except on an event of prior probability at most \(\varepsilon\).  Fixed-law honesty averaged under a prior therefore implies that \(C_n\) intersects the corresponding \(d/4\)-neighborhood with mixture probability at least \(1-\alpha-\varepsilon\).  Transferring one of these two events between mixtures costs at most \(\Gamma\).  On their intersection the interval meets two sets whose distance is at least \(2d-d/2=3d/2\).  Hence
\[
\overline P_-\{\operatorname{length}(C_n)\geq3d/2\}
\geq1-2\alpha-\Gamma-2\varepsilon.                     \qquad\text{(26)}
\]
The two-point amplitudes in the established converse may be fixed so that \(\Gamma\leq1/4\); in each fuzzy family its finite cell count may be enlarged until \(\Gamma+2\varepsilon\leq1/4\), without changing target separation or fixed-sign membership.  Since \(\alpha<1/4\), the right sides of (25)--(26) are bounded below by a positive constant.  A mixture expectation is an average of expectations under fixed-sign laws, so (26) implies that at least one fixed law in the corresponding family has expected interval length at least a positive constant times \(d\).

The four component target separations in \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse} are bounded below, up to fixed constants, by the four summands in \(\rho_n\).  If \(d_1,\ldots,d_4\) are these component scales, then
\[
\max_{1\leq j\leq4}d_j
\geq\frac14\sum_{j=1}^4d_j
\geq c\rho_n.                                           \qquad\text{(27)}
\]
Selecting the largest component in (27) and applying (25) or (26) proves, for every interval rule honest over \(\mathcal M_n\),
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}
E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_n)]
\geq c_\alpha\rho_n.                                   \qquad\text{(28)}
\]
Taking the infimum over honest rules in \texttt{def:bias-aware-interval}, and combining (28) with the upper bound (24) restricted through \(\mathcal M_n\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\), proves \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\) on the reservoir-rich class.  Only (21)--(24) were proved on the broader class; the lower bound (28) and the resulting equivalence use the two richness assumptions through \texttt{thm:four-channel-converse}.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), let \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\) denote the broader class obtained from \texttt{def:public-weak-overlap-class} by retaining all of its member conditions and deleting exactly \texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness} and \texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}.  The rule \(\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}\) from \texttt{def:clipped-score} and \texttt{def:oracle-threshold} belongs to \(\mathcal T_n\).  There is a constant \(C<\infty\), depending only on the retained fixed class constants, including \(M\) and \(\bar r\), such that
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
E_P\!\left|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)\right|
\leq C\rho_n.
\]
For every fixed \(\delta\in(0,1/4)\), the same estimator satisfies
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
P\!\left\{\left|\widehat\tau_{\lambda_n^{\star}}-\tau(P)\right|
>C\rho_n/\delta\right\}\leq\delta.
\]
Since \(\mathcal M_n\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\), both risk conclusions remain valid with \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\) replaced by the reservoir-rich class \(\mathcal M_n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The operator-directed maximality audit shows that the proof uses the uniform shell law but neither shell-richness inequality. The formal claim must record the proved broader upper-bound scope without changing the estimator, threshold, rate, or reservoir-rich corollary.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every admissible radius triple \((r_{0n},r_{1n},r_{en})\in[0,\bar r]^3\), let \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\) denote the broader class obtained from \texttt{def:public-weak-overlap-class} by retaining all of its member conditions and deleting exactly \texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness} and \texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}.  For every fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\), a choice of \(K_\alpha\) depending only on \(\alpha\), \(\bar r\), and the retained fixed class constants makes \(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\in\mathcal I_n\) uniformly honest on this broader class:
\[
\inf_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
P\{\tau(P)\in\mathcal C_{n,\alpha}\}\geq1-\alpha,
\qquad
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n}
E_P[\operatorname{length}(\mathcal C_{n,\alpha})]
\leq C_\alpha\rho_n.
\]
Conversely, when the reservoir-rich class \(\mathcal M_n\) is nonempty, every \(C_n\in\mathcal I_n\) that is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal M_n\), including every rule using the public functions and certified radii, satisfies
\[
\sup_{(P,m_0,m_1,p)\in\mathcal M_n}
E_P[\operatorname{length}(C_n)]\geq c_\alpha\rho_n.
\]
Consequently \(\mathfrak L_{n,\alpha}\asymp\rho_n\) on the reservoir-rich class.  No matching lower bound or length equivalence is asserted here for \(\widetilde{\mathcal M}_n\setminus\mathcal M_n\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The achievability proof inherits the broader scope of the clipped and median rules, whereas the expected-length converse uses the reservoir construction and therefore retains both richness conditions. The replacement separates those scopes and makes no broader converse claim.

prose_updates.tldr: The matched absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\), and honest expected-length for each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) frontiers at the four-channel rate \(\rho_n\) hold for fixed one-sided dyadic-shell constants satisfying both \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\). The clipped doubly robust estimator, five-block median amplification, and bias-aware interval upper bound need only the broader uniform one-sided-shell class obtained by deleting those two richness conditions. In the public-function experiment with bounded global \(L^2(P_X)\) certificates and a fixed conditional-effect signal envelope, the four channels are tail-amplified outcome noise, regression error hidden in shells with no treated observations, localized propensity--treated-regression uncertainty, and the regular control-side nuisance interaction. The reservoir-rich converse uses a complete atomic probability law and certifies every fixed-sign alternative, including the exact \(\kappa=1\) logarithm. Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.

project_justification.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR supplies WATE lower-bound templates in its estimator-bounded source class, whereas BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE supplies a lower-rate statement for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class. Neither published class is nested with the present dyadic-shell public-function experiment, so neither citation supports a class-inclusion argument or a transferred minimax theorem. Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than a finite-sample four-risk frontier. The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp results also have non-nested causal targets and law classes.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model isolates the statistical price of knowing only global prediction-error guarantees when treated observations vanish at a boundary. The estimator and interval upper bounds are valid on the full uniform one-sided-shell class, while the matching converse is certified on the reservoir-rich subclass satisfying both explicit shell-richness inequalities. The left tail creates three distinct treated-side obstructions, the control-side product remains regular, and \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\leq M\) keeps the ATE finite without a pointwise potential-outcome envelope.
project_justification.fill: The paper gives explicit clipped and median estimators and a bias-aware interval whose upper bounds use no reservoir-richness condition. On fixed shell constants satisfying both richness inequalities, an explicit law-by-law four-channel construction supplies the matching absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\), and honest expected-length for each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) lower bounds. Its dyadic background masses, signal-only localization cells, balancing companions, and completion masses form a complete probability law; fixed-sign shell membership, nuisance radii, moments, cancellation, collision control, and target separation are verified before the four scales are combined into \(\rho_n\).

prose_updates.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, gives squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bounds in its estimator-bounded source class. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, gives the lower-rate form \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\) for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class; the attested statement supplies neither a control-arm extension nor a joint two-arm ATE equivalence. Neither published class is nested with this note's dyadic-shell public-function experiment. Accordingly, the fast-tail calculation in \(\texttt{prop:regular-benchmark-reduction}\) is only an algebraic, source-scoped sanity comparison and proves no class inclusion, transferred lower bound, or transferred minimax equivalence. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics, MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, MaWang2020RobustIPW, and HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity study Gaussian or non-Gaussian inference, trimming, or threshold selection rather than this matched public-function minimax frontier. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies a fuzzy-hypothesis template for a different estimand and smoothness class; KhanTamer2010Irregular explains the tail-driven inverse-weight obstruction; Rothe2017RobustCI studies limited-overlap coverage under finite-cell or auxiliary structure. The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp papers likewise concern non-nested targets and law classes.

statement_notes.justification: It supplies one feasible procedure attaining all four upper-rate components on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class, without either reservoir-richness condition or stronger global \(L^2(P_X)\) information.
statement_notes.gap: Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves a sufficient studentized limit, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap gives asymptotic inference for a bias-corrected trimmed ATE procedure preserving the original target; neither establishes this finite-risk public-function upper frontier or its maximal uniform-shell scope.
statement_notes.consumer: Analysts with certified black-box prediction errors obtain a clipping rule for the original population ATE throughout the broader shell class, rather than a procedure whose validity depends on converse-side reservoir richness.

statement_notes.justification: The interval upper bound holds on the broader uniform-shell class, while the matching honest expected-length converse and equivalence are stated only on the reservoir-rich subclass where the four lower-bound families are certified.
statement_notes.gap: Rothe2017RobustCI uses finite-cell small-sample structure, Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics proves asymptotic Wald validity, and MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap proves asymptotic normality after bias-corrected trimming; none provides this global-\(L^2\) bias radius together with a reservoir-rich matching honest-length converse.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied work retaining the full population can report the bias-aware upper interval under the broader shell law, while reading minimax length optimality only under the explicitly stated richness conditions.
